records.text: Look at White's new passed pawn. No enemy pawn ahead on its file or the files beside it. Pieces can still stop it, though.
Look at Black's new passed pawn. No enemy pawn ahead on its file or the files beside it. Pieces can still stop it, though.
The better move would give White a passed pawn. No enemy pawn ahead on its file or either neighboring file. That's the change to spot.
The better move would give Black a passed pawn. No enemy pawn ahead on its file or either neighboring file. That's the change to spot.
White has an isolated pawn now. Where are its friendly pawns? None on the files next door.
Black has an isolated pawn now. Where are its friendly pawns? None on the files next door.

The better move would leave Black with an isolated pawn. No friendly pawns on the neighboring files, though pieces could still help.

Black's pawns are sharing a file now. Doubled pawns! That doesn't automatically make them bad.

Another move would leave Black's pawns sharing a file. They'd be doubled, not necessarily weak.

The better move would give Black's rook an open file. No pawns on that file at all, though pieces could still be there.

Black's rook has a half-open file. Its own pawns aren't on it, but enemy pawns are. That's what makes it half-open.
